experiments.design: 12 seeded trials x 100,000 synthetic cognitive requests. Requests require one of four evidence/resource tiers. Compare fixed low, fixed mid, fixed high and a noisy query-aware adaptive router with conservative escalation on uncertain cases.
experiments.inference: In the constructed demand model, operation/query-aware resource allocation can approach the fixed maximum-quality arm at substantially lower average resource cost. This validates the discriminating experiment shape for a FRANK Cognitive Resource Governor; it is not a real accuracy or energy estimate.
experiments.counter: A learned/adaptive router can itself become a failure source; target traces may favor a simpler fixed policy. Unknown/high-risk demand must therefore conservatively escalate.

experiments.design: 6 seeded trials x 80,000 episodes over 64 memory candidates. Candidate 0 is genuinely frequent for the first 15,000 episodes and then becomes ordinary. Compare naive exposure+reward reinforcement against bounded gain, faster decay, negative feedback for wrong selection, weak competition and periodic diversity reserve.
experiments.inference: The constructed regime demonstrates that truth-preserving utility learning can still create a self-reinforcing stale salience attractor. Bounded/adversarially-corrected salience policies can prevent the failure in this family.
experiments.boundary: Parameters intentionally create a sharp distribution shift to expose the mechanism. Magnitudes are not estimates of live ClayGraph behavior and do not establish the guarded policy as optimal. Diversity/inhibition may also suppress genuinely useful stable habits and needs target trade-off measurement.

negative_results: Maximal resource allocation is not justified merely because it yields the highest constructed quality; cost/latency/device shadows matter.
Utility adaptation that cannot write canonical truth can still create severe cognitive lock-in through salience feedback.
No current-run experiment measures live FRANK, target Qwen, Android thermal behavior, emergence or phenomenal consciousness.
